_doc: Drafted by the Profiler on issue #21 and re-verified on issue #54 against commit 011946f. Every command in `commands` was executed on a clean checkout in the repo's own Actions runner; every other field is cited to a file read or a command run in the PR body.
estate_role: Standalone. The Factory Console — a read-mostly lens and control panel over the Claude Software Factory (GitHub + OpenSpec), MIT-licensed and being prepared for public release (.github/REPOSITORY_SETTINGS.md). It has no sibling repos in this estate: it mirrors claude-software-factory's label/state contract in packages/core/src/factory.ts and forwards GitHub events to that repo's LangGraph orchestrator service over HTTP (packages/core/src/orchestrator-client.ts), but nothing in this estate depends on it and no code is shared, so there is no cross-repo merge order to honour.
stack: TypeScript end-to-end (ES2022, module NodeNext, strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess + noFallthroughCasesInSwitch), Node >=20.19, pnpm 10.33 workspace. apps/api = Fastify 5 (@fastify/cookie, GitHub OAuth, REST, webhook endpoint); apps/worker = BullMQ 5 on ioredis (webhook projection, reconciler, OpenSpec scaffolding, orchestrator forwarding); apps/web = React 18 + Vite 6 SPA (react-router-dom 6, @tanstack/react-query 5), unit-tested with Vitest + jsdom + Testing Library and carrying a Playwright 1.6 + @axe-core/playwright responsive/a11y harness in apps/web/e2e; packages/core = factory constants, hidden-comment markers, state derivation and per-state routing policy, two-token GitHub REST client (jose + libsodium-wrappers), AES-256-GCM envelope crypto, zod env config; packages/db = Drizzle ORM 0.36 over Postgres 16 (postgres.js driver) with hand-rolled forward-only SQL migrations; packages/insight = Anthropic SDK plus OpenAI-compatible providers for cited, read-only Q&A. Deployed as Docker images (infra/Dockerfile.api, infra/Dockerfile.web) behind nginx and Traefik on a VPS.
conventions: pnpm workspace, ESM only. Every package is `"type": "module"` and tsconfig is `module: NodeNext`, so relative imports MUST carry the `.js` extension even in TypeScript sources (`import { loadEpic } from "./read.js"`). Cross-package imports use the workspace aliases `@console/core`, `@console/db`, `@console/insight`.

API routes are `registerXRoutes(app: FastifyInstance, deps: AppDeps): void` in apps/api/src/routes/*.ts, wired once in apps/api/src/app.ts. Dependencies (config, db handle, credential store, BullMQ queues) are threaded through the `AppDeps` object — no module-level singletons, which is what lets the tests build the whole app against an in-process Postgres.

Every authenticated route starts with `const ctx = await requireAuth(deps, req, reply); if (!ctx) return;` and then scopes each query to `ctx.orgIds` at the data layer (`inArray(table.orgId, ctx.orgIds)`). Authorisation is a WHERE clause, not a post-filter. Errors are returned as `reply.code(N).send({ error: "lowercase message" })`.

Two-token model as a structural property (packages/core/src/github.ts): `InstallationClient` is the App's identity (reads, non-authoritative comments); `UserClient` is the human's OAuth identity. Anything carrying authority — approving, merging, labelling, filing issues — exists only on `UserClient` and is reached via `userClient(deps, ctx)`. Do not add an authoritative operation to `InstallationClient`.

Database access is Drizzle query-builder only (`db.select().from(x).where(and(eq(...)))`) — no raw SQL strings in app code. Schema lives in packages/db/src/schema.ts and is split by comment banner into GitHub PROJECTIONS (keyed by `gh_node_id`, guarded by `gh_updated_at`, rebuildable, never backed up) and CONSOLE-NATIVE tables. No table mixes the two.

Secrets are never stored in the clear: OAuth tokens, the GitHub App private key and cached repo content go through `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` (AES-256-GCM under `CONSOLE_MASTER_KEY`, `v1.iv.tag.ct` envelope). Environment variables are declared and validated in the zod schema in packages/core/src/config.ts and read as `cfg.X` — never `process.env` in app code.

Request bodies are validated by hand against Fastify's generic type parameters (`app.post<{ Body: {...} }>(...)` then explicit checks returning 400). zod is imported in exactly one source file, packages/core/src/config.ts, and is for environment config only; do not introduce a second body-validation style without saying so in design.md.

Anything the factory itself decides — which control the Console may offer, what a state means, what the next actor is — lives in packages/core as a pure function over labels and state, citing the FACTORY.md section it mirrors (`FACTORY.md §4b`), with a unit test of the same name in packages/core/test: epic-status.ts, next-step.ts, start-gate.ts, plan-tests.ts, test-verdict.ts, bug-report.ts, testing-policy.ts, expedite logic in derive.ts/phases.ts. A new factory rule goes there as a tested pure function, never inline in a route or a component — the Console renders factory state, it never invents it.

Comments explain *why*, not what: most modules open with a block comment citing the decision that shaped them — a plan or spec section (`spec 01 §2.2`, `plan 02 §1a`) for Console-native behaviour, a FACTORY.md section for anything mirroring the factory's own rules. New modules follow that — a reader should be able to get from the code to the decision behind it.

Anything the Console writes back to GitHub is an ordinary comment carrying a hidden marker (`<!-- console:thread=… -->`, `<!-- console:decision=… -->`, packages/core/src/markers.ts), built by `threadMarker()`/`decisionMarker()` rather than hand-written. That is what keeps the projection rebuildable and non-Console users first-class; never invent a new storage location for state that belongs on GitHub.

Tenant scoping has exactly one escape hatch: `systemScope()` in packages/db/src/index.ts, used by the reconciler and webhook workers because they act across tenants by design. It is deliberately greppable — cross-tenant access that does not go through it is a bug, and adding a second escape hatch defeats the audit.

The SPA talks to the API only through the `api.get/post/del` wrapper in apps/web/src/api.ts (same-origin credentials plus the `x-console-csrf` header on writes). Pages live in src/pages, shared widgets in src/components, cross-cutting helpers in src/lib, server state goes through TanStack Query; do not call `fetch()` directly from a component.
review_checklist: New or changed API route: does it call `requireAuth` and scope every query to `ctx.orgIds`? An unscoped `db.select()` in a route is a cross-tenant leak, and apps/api/test/memberships.test.ts exists because that boundary has been got wrong before.

State-changing route: it must be a non-GET method, so `requireAuth`'s CSRF-header check applies. A mutation behind `app.get` bypasses one of the two CSRF layers (there is deliberately no CORS — see the comment in apps/api/src/app.ts).

Authoritative GitHub operation (approve, merge, label, comment-as-user, file issue): must go through `userClient(deps, ctx)`, never `InstallationClient`. Check it also writes an `auditLog` row, as apps/api/src/routes/gate.ts and write.ts do.

Schema change: is there a new numbered file in packages/db/migrations/ (NNNN_name.sql, statements separated by `--> statement-breakpoint`)? The runner is forward-only and lexicographic — editing an already-applied migration is silently a no-op on any deployed database.

Projection change: does the write still guard on `gh_updated_at` (last-writer-wins) and key on `gh_node_id`? Webhook delivery is at-least-once and out of order; a projection write without the guard reintroduces flapping state.

Secrets: any new credential must be stored via `encryptSecret` and any new environment variable declared in the zod schema in packages/core/src/config.ts. A raw token column or a bare `process.env` read is a change request.

Factory label/state constants and routing rules in packages/core (factory.ts, derive.ts, phases.ts, start-gate.ts, next-step.ts, plan-tests.ts, test-verdict.ts, bug-report.ts) mirror claude-software-factory's FACTORY.md. Changing them to make the UI nicer desynchronises the Console from the factory; a rule the factory does not actually implement is a change request even when the UI reads better for it.
Markdown from GitHub must stay sanitised server-side (apps/api/src/render.ts uses marked + sanitize-html). Rendering untrusted markdown anywhere else, or relaxing the sanitiser, is a change request.

Any new comment body the Console can post to GitHub: confirm it cannot trim to exactly `Approved`, `Review Done`, `Test Passed`, `Test Failed` or `Plan tests` unless it is intentionally that control. Those five literals are declared in packages/core/src/factory.ts (APPROVED_BODY, REVIEW_DONE_BODY, TEST_PASSED_BODY, TEST_FAILED_BODY, PLAN_TESTS_BODY) because they are the factory router's live triggers, so an incidental match fires a real gate or verdict.

New or reshaped SPA surface: it must hold at 360, 768 and 1280px with no horizontal page pan and no new axe violation — the contract apps/web/e2e/ux.spec.ts asserts. CI does not run that suite (see qa_notes), so a reviewer who cannot see the change rendered should ask for `pnpm --filter @console/web test:e2e` output rather than assume it.
qa_notes: Vitest 2 throughout; `pnpm test` runs `pnpm -r test` across the workspace and is green on a clean checkout (verified at 011946f: all six packages pass, 1m52s wall). Tests live either in a `test/` directory beside `src/` (apps/api 25 files / 249 tests, packages/core 15, apps/worker 6, packages/insight 1) or beside the module they cover (apps/web, 11 `*.test.ts(x)` files under src/), all named `*.test.ts(x)`.

Only packages/db (0 test files) and packages/insight run vitest with `--passWithNoTests`. apps/web no longer does: it has a real jsdom suite (`environment: "jsdom"`, `setupFiles: ./src/test-setup.ts` which wires @testing-library/jest-dom and an `afterEach(cleanup)`), configured in apps/web/vite.config.ts rather than a separate vitest.config.ts. Component tests use @testing-library/react and user-event.

Integration tests boot a real in-process Postgres (`new PGlite()` from @electric-sql/pglite, drizzle-orm/pglite adapter) and apply every file in packages/db/migrations in `beforeAll`, then build the whole Fastify app via `buildApp(deps)`. See apps/api/test/security.test.ts for the canonical setup and apps/worker/test/helpers.ts for the worker equivalent. No Docker, no external database — a new suite should follow the same shape rather than mocking the database.

GitHub is never called for real: tests point `apiUrl` at `https://api.invalid` and inject fakes through `AppDeps` (e.g. `CredentialStore({ load: async () => null })` to exercise the environment fallback). Queues are replaced with in-memory arrays that record what was enqueued.

That PGlite warmup is why apps/api/vitest.config.ts and apps/worker/vitest.config.ts raise `testTimeout` to 30s (and the API's `hookTimeout` to 60s). A new suite that boots its own PGlite instance needs the same allowance.

apps/web has a second suite that `pnpm test` does NOT run and CI does not run either: `pnpm --filter @console/web test:e2e` (apps/web/playwright.config.ts → e2e/ux.spec.ts). It serves a standalone harness page (e2e.html → e2e/harness.tsx, screens selected by `?screen=`) on 127.0.0.1:4177 via its own `webServer`, then asserts at 360/768/1280px that no page pans horizontally and that axe finds no violation. It needs browsers installed (`pnpm exec playwright install`), which this run did not have, so it was read rather than executed. CONTRIBUTING.md asks contributors to run it for UI changes.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, and the identical gate in deploy.yml) runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm test` on every branch and PR, with a read-only `contents: read` token. Typecheck is a real gate — a PR that compiles under `tsc --noEmit` in one package but not another still fails CI. Separately, .github/workflows/codeql.yml runs CodeQL over `javascript-typescript` and `actions` on pushes and PRs to main and weekly; a new finding there shows as a code-scanning alert, not as a failed CI job.

apps/worker/test carries the projection invariants, including an explicit replay test — 'is idempotent and order-tolerant: shuffled + duplicated replay converges to the same state'. Any change to apps/worker/src/project.ts must keep that green and, if it adds a projected entity, extend it rather than adding a separate happy-path test.
gotchas: There is no linter or formatter in this repo — no eslint, prettier or biome config, and no package declares a `lint` script. The root `package.json` does have `"lint": "pnpm -r lint"`, but running it FAILS with `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT` (re-verified at 011946f, exit 1). `commands.lint` is null for that reason: treat a red `pnpm lint` as the absence of a gate, not as a defect introduced by your change.

`pnpm test` is slow — 1m52s wall clock measured on a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner, with apps/api alone taking ~67s (249 tests) and apps/worker ~37s, because nearly every test there boots a fresh PGlite Postgres and replays every migration. It is not hung; budget for it rather than killing it. Do not speed it up by cutting the vitest timeouts.

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is required: pnpm-lock.yaml is committed and CI uses the frozen flag, so a dependency added without updating the lockfile fails CI at the install step, before any test output exists to explain it. Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) opens weekly npm, Actions and Docker updates, so expect lockfile churn from PRs you did not open.
Relative imports need the `.js` extension (NodeNext). Omitting it typechecks in some editors but fails `tsc -p tsconfig.json` and at runtime — this is the single most common build break here.

packages/db's build copies `migrations/` into `dist/migrations` as a second step; a migration added without running `pnpm build` is invisible to `runMigrations` in a built (Docker) image even though the tests, which read the source directory directly, pass.

The api and worker both run `runMigrations` on boot and would race, so the runner takes a Postgres advisory lock (packages/db/src/migrate.ts). Do not 'simplify' that lock away — without it Postgres fails one process with a duplicate-key error on pg_type_typname_nsp_index.

The webhook route deliberately sits outside session/CSRF middleware and reads the raw body in `preParsing` for HMAC verification. Moving it behind the normal request pipeline, or letting JSON parsing consume the body first, breaks signature verification for every delivery.

A stale Vite artifact is committed: `apps/web/vite.config.ts.timestamp-1786244617305-2049876fd0fad.mjs` is tracked in git (verified with `git ls-files`) and .gitignore does not cover the pattern. Vite regenerates these on every config load, so `git add -A` or `git add apps/web` will sweep a fresh one into your PR. Stage files explicitly, and do not delete the tracked one as a drive-by — it is its own fix.

The factory pipeline will not start an agent for an issue opened by someone without write access: the caller stub's job-level `if:` requires an OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR author, a Bot sender, or a label applied by someone other than the author (.github/workflows/factory-pipeline.yml, and CONTRIBUTING.md says so to contributors). An outside contributor's issue therefore sits with no factory state until a maintainer labels it — that is intended, not a stuck pipeline.

GitHub forbids Actions secret names starting with `GITHUB_`, so the deploy workflow takes `GH_APP_*` / `GH_OAUTH_*` and writes them to the VPS `.env` as `GITHUB_APP_*` / `GITHUB_OAUTH_*`. Also: those values must come from `env_file` only — adding `${GITHUB_APP_*}` to a compose `environment:` block blanks them via empty interpolation (noted in the deploy workflow and infra/docker-compose.deploy.yml).
`DEV_FAKE_LOGIN=1` bypasses GitHub OAuth entirely. It is a local-development switch and must never reach a deployed environment.

The integration branch named by `.github/factory-branches.json` (`staging`, `required: true`, `auto_create: true`) does not exist in this repo yet — re-verified against the full paginated branch list at 011946f, which holds only `main`, agent branches and Dependabot branches. `auto_create` means the first factory run that needs it cuts it from `main`. Base task and fast-track PRs on `staging`, not on `main`; a PR based on `main` is a review finding (FACTORY.md §6a). The policy file sets no `epics` key, so there are no per-epic branches and document PRs also target `staging`.

There is no staging *deployment*. .github/workflows/deploy.yml fires only on push to `main` (verified: `on: push: branches: [main]`, plus workflow_dispatch), so merging onto `staging` deploys nothing and the health checks below cannot be run against a staging environment — 'verified on staging' here means CI green on that branch, nothing more. The real deploy is the promotion merge to `main`.

.github/workflows/deploy.yml also has no `paths-ignore`, so EVERY push to `main` runs a full production deploy, including a documents-only promotion merge. Do not merge anything to `main` when production must stay still.
reuse_hotspots: packages/core/src — before adding a helper, check here: factory.ts (label/state constants and comment-trigger literals), markers.ts (hidden-comment parse/emit), derive.ts and phases.ts (factory state derivation), epic-status.ts / next-step.ts / start-gate.ts / plan-tests.ts / test-verdict.ts / bug-report.ts / testing-policy.ts (per-state policy as pure functions, each with a test of the same name), orchestrator.ts and orchestrator-client.ts (engine choice and event forwarding), crypto.ts (envelope encrypt/decrypt), config.ts (env schema), github.ts (the whole REST surface, App JWT and OAuth), credentials.ts (App credential resolution, database-first with env fallback). It is re-exported wholesale from packages/core/src/index.ts.

apps/api/src/context.ts — `requireAuth`, `resolveSession`, `userClient` and the `AppDeps`/`RequestCtx` types. Any new route needs these rather than its own auth path. apps/api/src/gh-write.ts and user-token.ts hold the shared write and token-renewal paths.
apps/api/src/routes/read.ts — `loadEpic` and the epic/repo/org lookup helpers other route modules already import. apps/api/src/render.ts is the single markdown sanitiser.

packages/db/src/schema.ts — 30 tables; check for an existing one before adding another. Several concerns that look separate already have homes here: threads/threadEntries, decisions, gateViews, gateAssignments, auditLog, webhookDeliveries (the idempotency ledger), reconcileRuns, notifications, orchestratorSecrets, artifactCache, changes/changeArtifacts.

apps/worker/src/artifacts.ts and project.ts — projection and repair helpers (`refreshRepoProfile`, `repairDependencies`, `projectIssue`, `projectPull`, …) reused by both the ingest worker and the reconciler; reconcile.ts and openspec.ts hold the sweep and scaffolding jobs.

apps/web/src/api.ts (the fetch wrapper with the CSRF header and the `needsReauth` distinction), apps/web/src/lib/ (board.ts, filter.tsx, labels.ts, reauth.ts), apps/web/src/theme.ts and apps/web/src/components/ — the SPA's shared pieces; pages should compose these rather than re-implement fetching, filtering or label rendering.

health_checks: curl -fsS "${PUBLIC_ORIGIN:-https://sf.genaipeople.com}/api/health"   # expects {"ok":true,"service":"console-api"} — the route is registered in apps/api/src/app.ts. The authoritative origin is the PUBLIC_ORIGIN variable on the `production` GitHub Environment; the fallback here is the value documented in deploy.yml and the README, not one this run could confirm against a live host.
ssh $DEPLOY_USER@$DEPLOY_HOST 'cd ~/factory-console && docker compose ps'   # every service up; postgres and redis report healthy
notes: These checks only ever describe production. There is no staging deployment (see gotchas), so after an integration merge onto `staging` the only available evidence is CI on that branch — do not report a staging health check that was not run.

Deploy is .github/workflows/deploy.yml on push to main (or Run workflow): typecheck+build+test gate, then build both images, scp tarballs to the VPS, docker load, docker compose up in ~/factory-console. A merge to main IS the production deploy.

The workflow's own gate polls the api container for `healthy` for 3 minutes and fails the deploy if it never gets there, dumping `docker compose ps` and the last 100 api log lines. That failure halts the release: the previous containers are already gone by then, so the site is down until it is fixed or rolled back.

Migrations run automatically at api and worker boot. A migration that fails leaves the api container unhealthy and the deploy red — check the api logs first when a deploy fails immediately after a schema change.

The deploy pre-flight refuses to run unless every one of DEPLOY_HOST, DEPLOY_USER, DEPLOY_KEY, CONSOLE_MASTER_KEY, DB_PASSWORD, PUBLIC_ORIGIN, GH_APP_ID, GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, GH_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, GH_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GH_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET is set on the `production` GitHub Environment.

CONSOLE_MASTER_KEY must never be rotated casually: it decrypts every stored OAuth token, the GitHub App private key and the artifact cache. Losing or changing it means every user must sign in again and the App must be re-registered.

Traefik routes Host(CONSOLE_HOST) on the shared `lighthouse-network` docker network to this stack's nginx. If that network or the Traefik instance is missing, the containers come up healthy and the site is still unreachable — check from outside, not only from the host.
